I'm working with a Laravel permissions package and I keep running into an ergonomics problem: I can only assign or remove roles from the user's side, but there's no way to do it from the role's side.

*   The Role model must expose a syncModels method that replaces all existing model-role associations for that role with the given set of models; models that were previously assigned but are absent from the new set must lose the role, and models in the new set must gain it.

*   When syncModels is called with an empty collection or array, all existing model-role associations for the role must be removed.

*   syncModels must deduplicate its inputs — passing the same model instance or the same ID more than once must result in exactly one pivot record, not multiple.

*   The Role model must expose an assignToModels method that grants the role to the given models without touching any existing assignments; models that already have the role must not gain a duplicate pivot record.

*   assignToModels must be idempotent: calling it repeatedly for the same model produces exactly one pivot record in the model_has_roles table.

*   assignToModels must deduplicate inputs: passing the same model or ID twice in a single call creates only one pivot record.

*   The Role model must expose a removeFromModels method that revokes the role from the given models while leaving all other role assignments untouched; calling it for a model that does not have the role must produce no error and no change.

*   All three methods (syncModels, assignToModels, removeFromModels) must accept any of the following as their first argument: a single Eloquent model instance, a single integer or string ID, an array of model instances, an array of IDs, or a mixed array of model instances and IDs.

*   All three methods accept an optional second argument that is the fully-qualified model class name; when raw IDs are passed as the first argument and a class name is supplied as the second argument, that class is used to resolve the IDs to model records.

*   When raw IDs are passed without an explicit model class, the methods must fall back to the value of the permission.models.default_model configuration key (if set) to determine which model class to use for resolving those IDs.

*   The HasAssignedModels trait must be used by the Role model so that all three methods are available on Role instances.

# `HasAssignedModels` Trait — Method Analysis

This is Spatie Permission open-source code (MIT-licensed). The trait lets a role manage which polymorphic models it's assigned to.

## Imports (use statements)

```php
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\MorphToMany;
use Illuminate\Database\Query\Builder;
use Illuminate\Support\Arr;
use Illuminate\Support\Collection;
use Spatie\Permission\PermissionRegistrar;
use Spatie\Permission\Support\Config;
```

- `Model` — type-hints for Eloquent models passed in.
- `MorphToMany` — return type of the polymorphic relation.
- `Builder` (Query) — return type for the raw query helper.
- `Arr` — used for `Arr::flatten` and `Arr::wrap`.
- `Collection` — accepted input type.
- `PermissionRegistrar` — resolved via `app()` to read `pivotRole`.
- `Config` — accessor for table names, morph keys, and team settings.

---

## `assignToModels(...)`
Adds assignments without deleting existing ones.

**Logic:** If the role doesn't yet exist in DB (`! $this->exists`), it returns early. Otherwise it computes the team pivot, then for each morph-class group it builds the relation, reads the already-attached IDs via `pluck(Config::morphKey())`, and attaches only the difference (`array_diff`). Finally clears the `users` cached relation.

```
if (!exists) return $this
teamPivot = teamPivot()
foreach (grouped models as class => ids):
    relation = relationForModel(class)
    existing = relation.pluck(morphKey)
    relation.attach(diff(ids, existing), teamPivot)
unsetRelation('users')
```

Query calls: `pluck`, `attach`. Teams handled via `$teamPivot` passed into `attach`.

---

## `removeFromModels(...)`
Detaches assignments.

**Logic:** For each grouped class, calls `detach($ids)` on the relation, then clears the `users` relation. No existence check, no team pivot needed.

```
foreach (grouped models as class => ids):
    relationForModel(class).detach(ids)
unsetRelation('users')
```

Query calls: `detach`.

---

## `syncModels(...)`
Replaces all current assignments with the given set.

**Logic:** If the role exists, it deletes all existing pivot rows for the role first (`newPivotQueryForRole()->delete()`). Then it attaches every grouped ID (no dedup against existing rows, since they were just wiped), applying the team pivot.

```
if (exists): newPivotQueryForRole().delete()
teamPivot = teamPivot()
foreach (grouped models as class => ids):
    relationForModel(class).attach(ids, teamPivot)
unsetRelation('users')
```

Query calls: raw `delete`, `attach`.

---

## `relationForModel(string $modelClass): MorphToMany`
Builds a polymorphic relation for a specific target class.

**Logic:** Returns `morphedByMany` using the model class, `'model'` morph name, the model-has-roles table, the pivot role column from the registrar, and `Config::morphKey()` as the related key.

```
return morphedByMany(class, 'model', modelHasRolesTable, pivotRole, morphKey)
```

---

## `groupModelsByMorphClass(...)`
Normalizes and groups input into `[class => [ids]]`.

**Logic:** Resolves a default class (for raw IDs). Flattens and wraps the input into one collection, rejects `null`/empty-string values, then reduces: if a value is a `Model` it uses `$value::class` and `$value->getKey()`; otherwise the default class and the raw value. It only appends an ID if not already present for that class using a strict `in_array` check — this is the deduplication mechanism, per-class.

```
default = resolveDefaultModelClass(modelClass)
collect(flatten(wrap(models)))
  .reject(null or '')
  .reduce((grouped, value):
      class = value is Model ? value::class : default
      id    = value is Model ? value.getKey() : value
      if id not strictly in grouped[class]:
          grouped[class][] = id
      return grouped)
```

Grouping is by morph class; deduplication is strict (type-aware) and scoped to each class.

---

## `resolveDefaultModelClass(?string $modelClass): string`
Chooses the class for raw ID inputs.

**Logic:** Uses the explicit argument if provided, else `config('permission.models.default_model')`, else falls back to `getModelForGuard()` using the role's own `guard_name` attribute or the default auth guard.

```
return modelClass
    ?? config('permission.models.default_model')
    ?? getModelForGuard(guard_name ?? default guard)
```

---

## `teamPivot(): array`
Provides extra pivot data when teams are enabled.

**Logic:** If teams are disabled (`! Config::teamsEnabled()`), returns an empty array. Otherwise returns an array mapping the team foreign key to the current team ID from `getPermissionsTeamId()`.

```
if (!teamsEnabled) return []
return [teamForeignKey => getPermissionsTeamId()]
```

---

## `newPivotQueryForRole(): Builder`
Raw query for this role's pivot rows.

**Logic:** Uses the model's connection, targets the model-has-roles table, and filters where the pivot role column equals this role's key. Used by `syncModels` to bulk-delete.

```
return connection
    .table(modelHasRolesTable)
    .where(pivotRole, this.getKey())
```

---

## Teams summary
Teams affect only **writes that attach** (`assignToModels`, `syncModels`) via `teamPivot()`, which injects `[teamForeignKey => teamId]` into `attach`. Detach and the raw delete query don't add team scoping in this trait.

## Summary

Added role-side bulk model-assignment operations to the spatie/laravel-permission package.

**New file — `src/Traits/HasAssignedModels.php`** — a trait providing three public methods on the `Role` model:

- **`assignToModels($models, $modelClass = null)`** — grants the role to the given models without touching existing assignments. It plucks the already-attached pivot IDs per model class and only attaches the difference (`array_diff`), making it idempotent and duplicate-free.
- **`removeFromModels($models, $modelClass = null)`** — detaches the role from the given models only; `detach` on absent rows is a safe no-op.
- **`syncModels($models, $modelClass = null)`** — deletes all existing pivot rows for the role (raw query), then attaches the new set. An empty input leaves the role with no associations.

Supporting private/protected helpers:
- `groupModelsByMorphClass()` — flattens/wraps any accepted input (single model, single ID, arrays, Collections, mixed), rejects null/empty values, and reduces into `[class => [ids]]` with strict per-class deduplication.
- `resolveDefaultModelClass()` — resolves raw IDs using the explicit `$modelClass`, then `permission.models.default_model` config, then `getModelForGuard()` for the role's guard.
- `relationForModel()` — builds the `morphedByMany` pivot relation for a given class.
- `teamPivot()` — injects the team foreign key on attaching writes when teams are enabled.
- `newPivotQueryForRole()` — raw query on `model_has_roles` scoped to this role.

**`src/Models/Role.php`** — imported and `use`d the `HasAssignedModels` trait so all three methods are available on `Role` instances.

All accept the full union type `array|Collection|Model|int|string` for the first argument as specified. Lint passes and the existing 48 Models tests still pass.
